thread:
sara.k: I think I clicked an 'Approve app' email from what looked like IT. The button said 'Allow TimeTracker Pro'. I clicked before I realized it might be spoofed. Link: https://timetrackr-app.example/consent

alex.g: don't click anything else. can you paste the full email headers and the exact link (no more clicks)? also which account did you approve it from?

sara.k: forwarding headers (redacted) — From: it-notify@redwood-support.com
Subject: Action required: Approve app for company
Link: https://timetrackr-app.example/consent?client_id=abc123&redirect=https://app.redwood.com/callback
clicked at ~2026-03-20 10:12am PT

mike.r: that domain is a typo of timetracker -> timetrackr (missing k). looks like an OAuth consent flow. we need to check if any tokens were minted for sara.k. @sec-ops-bot can you run an app-consent-scan for sara.k and the client_id abc123?

sec-ops-bot: Running app-consent-scan for sara.k (client_id=abc123)...
- Found OAuth grant: client_id=abc123, app_name="TimeTracker Pro", scopes=[User.Read, Mail.Read], granted_at=2026-03-20T17:12:34Z
- Action: revoking grant...
- Revoke command status: success (revoked grant id g-0a1b2c)

mike.r: revoked and blacklisted that client_id from our tenant. good catch. next: force SSO session reset for sara.k, rotate any app credentials that might be associated, and scan mailbox for exfil. olivia.p can you reset sessions and enforce admin-consent policy for new apps?

olivia.p: resetting SSO sessions for sara.k now. also creating a policy change request to require admin consent for non-whitelisted apps. sara, please do not follow any links in the original email — forward the raw message to sec@redwood.com instead of clicking. we'll send password reset instructions via the console (not via email).

sara.k: thanks. forwarded original to sec@redwood.com. no outgoing mail observed in my Sent. laptop still online. :grimacing:

alex.g: @sec-ops-bot run mailbox-audit for sara.k for the last 24h and surface any large attachments or external forwarding rules created.

sec-ops-bot: Mailbox audit complete for sara.k:
- No large attachments sent (>10MB)
- No new forwarding rules found
- 2 failed/blocked sign-in attempts from RU IP ranges; MFA prevented session creation
- No outbound bulk send detected

mike.r: good. containment looks successful. post-incident actions:
- Add detection for 'allowlist/approve' phrasing in vendor emails and suspicious domain similarity (typosquatting)
- Company comms reminder: do NOT approve app consents unless requested by IT; share examples
- Enforce Admin Consent Required for non-whitelisted apps (policy request filed)
- 1:1 awareness with sara.k to walk through what happened

olivia.p: I'll draft the short comms now and put the policy request in the infra backlog. Also scheduling a quick review with Identity team tomorrow to enable 'block high-risk consent' rule.

sara.k: thanks everyone. appreciate the quick responses. keep me posted if you need anything from my side.

mike.r: filing incident INF-2026-092 with notes and attaching mail headers + revoked grant ids. we'll follow up in the incident tracker with remediation verification and a short retrospective. :white_check_mark:
